newsitem.title: UK: First Leisure says H2 trading disappoints.
newsitem.headline: First Leisure says H2 trading disappoints.

text.p: First Leisure, the British operator of discotheques, visitor attractions, bingo halls and hotels, said on Tuesday trading in the first few weeks of the second half of the year had fallen slightly short of expectations.
The group blamed some good weather in May for slower trading in the early part of the second half, which it said did not help its indoor business.

First Leisure, which earlier reported a slip in first half pre-tax profits to 17.2 million stg -- the top-end of expectations -- said each of its divisions, with the exception of bingo, had achieved good growth in both sales and profits.

After board changes, including Michael Grade becoming full-time chairman and chief executive John Colan announcing he would leave, First Leisure said costs including a restructuring of its bingo halls would result in an exceptional 2.4 million stg charge in the year.

Although comparable sales in the group's three largest divisions are ahead of last year, it said its bingo division was still not recovering. At current trading levels, it is expected to report flat results in the second half.

"We have challenges -- in particular improving the performance of bingo -- but sat the same time considerable opportunities," Grade said in the results statement. "Overall, I look forward to the future with confidence."
